ramble.description: I own Peaches, Ramble's meeting agent. Python on the server, TypeScript and React on the web, Swift on Mac and iPhone. Internal beta. No outside users yet.
ramble.longDescription: Peaches sits in the meeting. You wake it, it joins from the calendar, it keeps a session, it writes notes and checklists. I own that product. Python services, the web client, the Mac app, the iPhone app. Other engineers review and test. Nobody outside the company uses it yet.
responsibilities: Owned Peaches end to end: Python backend, TypeScript and React web client, native Swift on macOS and iPhone
Built the voice loop: wake and sleep, transcript buffering, session context, tools that write notes and checklists
Ran meeting-bot lifecycle and calendar auto-join: durable persistence, short-lived credentials, verified webhooks, background reconciliation
Shipped cross-device control from macOS: presence, acknowledgements, failure-state feedback
Shipped the iPhone app: on-device transcription, session history, editable notes, bounded real-time audio
achievements: Took Peaches from a prototype to an internal beta on Mac, iPhone, and web
Calendar auto-join can run without someone watching the bot
Native apps, web, and backend share one session model

thinking-lab.description: Three-person software company in Sylhet. First product is HealthERP, a hospital system. We also take custom software work.
thinking-lab.longDescription: Thinking Lab is me, Mehedi Hasan Rumi, and Fazle Rabbi Rakib. Small company, Sylhet. We build software for operations that off-the-shelf tools don't fit. HealthERP is the first product: patients, appointments, pharmacy, billing, lab, admin, in one place. The site is up. The product is still being built.
responsibilities: Co-founded the company with a three-person team
Building HealthERP, covering patients, appointments, pharmacy, billing, laboratory, and administration
Talking to hospitals about the actual workflow before we draw a screen
Writing custom software for businesses whose ops live in too many tools
achievements: HealthERP is the founding product and is in active development

ponno.description: Founding engineer on a three-person team. RAG over product and order data, tool-calling agents, the first architecture. Work finished in 2026.
ponno.longDescription: Ponno needed a way to turn messy buyer messages into catalog lookups and orders. I was the founding engineer on a team of three. We built retrieval on pgVector and ChromaDB, and tool-calling with the Vercel AI SDK so the agent could take the next step instead of only chatting. I left after the architecture and the first working path were in place.
responsibilities: Built a retrieval layer on pgVector and ChromaDB that maps messy intent onto product and order data
Made tool-calling reliable when schemas drifted, context ran out, or the model invented a parameter
Set code review and architecture habits for a three-person engineering team
achievements: Left a working retrieval and tool-calling path, not a slide deck
Three-person team, with review and architecture in place

edgep-instructor.description: Taught Python and a bit of machine learning to more than 100 students at three universities.
edgep-instructor.longDescription: EDGE is an ICT Division program, World Bank money. I taught Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and a first pass at regression and clustering. Students from SUST, Jagannath, and Stamford. One of the rooms was the same one where I sat my first programming class.
responsibilities: Lectures on Python, pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn
Regression, clustering, and classification, at undergrad pace
A small Flask UI so the models weren't just notebooks
More than 100 students across three universities
achievements: Taught in the room where I learned to code

traders-connect.description: Native Swift talking to gRPC, a React Native component library, and a 20+ screen trading app.
traders-connect.longDescription: Contract work on a trading product that was still finding its feet. I wrote Swift modules so React Native could talk to a gRPC server, built a reusable component library, and shipped a mobile app with more than 20 screens. OAuth for login.
responsibilities: Native Swift modules bridging React Native to a gRPC server
Reusable React Native components with styled-components
Mobile app, 20+ screens
OAuth login
Early front-end setup for the web app
achievements: Swift and React Native talking over gRPC without a mess of glue

recruit.description: The job that turned into Ramble. I built the AI resume product, the tests, and the login.
recruit.longDescription: This is where I started with this team. Next.js, Postgres, Prisma, OpenAI for resume text, Playwright and Jest, Magic Link for auth. A Python corpus tester on the side. That product line became Ramble.
responsibilities: Resume builder in Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma, Postgres, with OpenAI for the writing
Jest and Playwright suites
Magic Link auth
Python tools for corpus testing
achievements: Resume product people could actually finish

kaz-software.description: 40+ pages, two UIs, a React 16 to 18 upgrade, and four apps mashed into Single-SPA.
kaz-software.longDescription: Kaz was a lot of React. I designed over 40 pages for an app with two different interfaces, moved two codebases from React 16 to 18, merged four apps into one Single-SPA shell, put Docker around deploys, and wrote Cypress tests. Unromantic work. The kind that ships.
responsibilities: 40+ pages, two UIs, React, TypeScript, SWR, Redux Toolkit, RSuite, SCSS
React 16 to 18 on two apps
Four React apps into one Single-SPA micro-frontend
Docker for deploys
Cypress end-to-end tests
achievements: 40+ pages live on a dual-interface product

bengali-ai.description: A React dashboard for comparing Bengali text-to-speech models, wired to Python over WebSocket.
bengali-ai.longDescription: Bengali.AI needed a way to put speech models in front of people. I built a React app that could benchmark Bengali TTS models, and a Flask server that pushed audio and scores over WebSocket so you didn't wait on a full page reload.
responsibilities: React app for comparing Bengali TTS models
Flask wrapper so the models could talk to the browser over WebSocket
achievements: Researchers could click a model and hear it, in the browser
